newsitem.title: UK: Market's bullish zinc outlook overdone-broker.
newsitem.headline: Market's bullish zinc outlook overdone-broker.

text.p: Zinc prices may spike up at some point this year but the market's widely-held bullish view is overdone, broker GNI said in a report.

"GNI believes that 1997 will be an uninspiring year for zinc. While we would love to believe the growing market consensus for a sharply improved zinc price in 1997, current evidence tells us to remain cautious," the broker said in its Outlook 1997 report.

A fund-led speculative flurry could push London Metal Exchange (LME) three month prices up to a peak of $1,240 per tonne late this year, but they will likely spend most of 1997 in a $1,040-$1,120 range.
The average price for 1997 is seen around $1,100.
On Tuesday, prices rose to about $1,080 per tonne after stocks data showed LME inventories dropped to the lowest level since December 1992.
The market deficit is expected to narrow in 1997 to 51,000 tonnes from 128,000 tonnes the previous year, with China a critical producer.
"Low prices and concentrate shortages have restrained Chinese production in 1996, however, the country's production potential will be enormous over the next few years," the report said.
Nickel prices are expected to fluctuate between $6,400 and $8,000 during much of the year, averaging at $6,800 to $7,000.
"However, should the recent buying dry up as quickly as it started, and growth figures start to look recessive, then there is the propensity for prices to dip to around $5,800," GNI said.
LME prices gained nearly 10 percent last week on a short-covering rally and hovered just under $7,250 on Tuesday.
The report forecasts a supply surplus of 17,000 tonnes in 1997 after a 35,000 tonne surplus the previous year.

"While some of the excess could be eroded by strong economic growth, the risks of a sharp rise in price in 1997 appear small; it would take consumption growth of six percent to balance the market and around nine percent to wipe out the 1996 excess," GNI said.
In the lead market, LME stocks will be the key to price action.
"Given that world lead stocks are at critical levels, the market could actually be surprised by the strength of demand in the first quarter of 1997," GNI said.
If stocks start to reverse their upward trend, prices could react quickly.
A seasonal dip in prices is likely in the summer months, possibly as low as $650, before they begin to rise at year end.
Prices are likely to range from $850 to $650, with an average of $750.
